subject: Capacity bridge proposal + updated rate card for AtlasAI renewal
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen@atlasai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AtlasAI renewal — usage snapshot + capacity bridge proposal

Hi Helen —

Thanks again for the time on Tuesday. We pulled a short usage snapshot and built a capacity-bridge option that lets AtlasAI lock in the performance profile you rely on while smoothing month-to-month spend as usage grows. Key highlights in the attached:

- Current run-rate: ~1.8B tokens/month (3-month median).
- Observed 18% month-over-month growth on inference requests tied to your recommendations engine.
- Suggested committed uplifts: +40% tokens for Q1 (to cover forecasted surge) with an optional step-down if usage normalizes.

Proposal (preview attachments):
- 12-month amendment (starts 2027-01-01) with a two-step commit corridor: 40% for months 1–3, 25% for months 4–12.
- Rate card: discounted unit price for committed tokens; uncommitted usage billed at base hosted rate.
- One-time migration credit to offset quantization effort if you move the latency-critical endpoints to our Dedicated pool.

Attachments: atlas_usage_nov_preview.csv, capacity_bridge_offer_v2.docx, rate_card_2027.pdf

Would love to get your high-level thoughts this week. If it helps, we can also propose a one-page mutual action plan for procurement.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

From: Helen Park <helen@atlasai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Doshi <samir@atlasai.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasAI renewal — usage snapshot + capacity bridge proposal

Thanks Monica — good summary and helpful attachments. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we loop procurement:

1) For the 40% uplift months, is there a pro-rata true-up if actual usage ends up 25% over the committed amount? We want to avoid large overage spikes.
2) The migration credit — is that a bill credit or an engineering time reimbursement? If it's credit, how is it amortized?
3) Can you confirm latency SLOs if we move 3 critical endpoints to Dedicated? We need <90ms p95 for those.

If those items look okay we can schedule a procurement sync next week.

- Helen
Helen Park
Head of Product Operations, AtlasAI
helen@atlasai.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: AtlasAI renewal — capacity bridge questions

Looping Lauren for quick pricing/credit speak. Customer asked about overage true-ups and how we handle migration credits. My take: we can offer a capped overage tiering (1.0–1.25x at committed rate + small premium, >1.25x at standard overage) and present migration credit as a one-time invoice credit (applied in first billing cycle post-migration). Need approval on credit max and whether to include a time-limited DocuSign amendment offering.

Marcus

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasAI renewal — capacity bridge questions

Agree with Marcus on structure. Approve the following for the commercial ask:

- Migration credit: invoice credit up to $24,000 applied in month 1 after migration (do not exceed 10% of ARR).
- Overage tiers: 0–1x committed: covered; 1.0–1.25x: billed at committed unit price + 8% premium; >1.25x: billed at public overage rate.
- DocuSign: yes — send a 7-day hold-open amendment (capacity_bridge_offer_v2.docx) once customer confirms in writing.

Monica — you have authority to make this offer and to coordinate with procurement. Capture acceptance via DocuSign link and loop legal for finalization.

Lauren
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen@atlasai.com>, Samir Doshi <samir@atlasai.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2026 13:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasAI renewal — usage snapshot + capacity bridge proposal

Hi Helen / Samir —

Thanks for the quick questions — confirm the following:

- True-up / overage: we'll apply the tiering Lauren authorized (1.0–1.25x at committed+8%, >1.25x at public rate). This protects you from sudden billing cliffs while preserving predictable unit economics.
- Migration credit: one-time invoice credit of up to $24,000, applied on the first invoice after migration completion. If migration doesn't happen, credit is not issued.
- Latency SLOs: Dedicated pool with your three endpoints pinned will meet <90ms p95 in our benchmarks; I'll attach a short latency note. If you'd like, we can run a short-stint test on a Dedicated node before migration.

Attached: capacity_bridge_offer_v2.docx (7-day hold open), rate_card_2027.pdf

Next step: if procurement is comfortable, I can send the DocuSign amendment (7-day window) and a mutual action plan to outline migration milestones.

Regards,
Monica

From: Helen Park <helen@atlasai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>, Samir Doshi <samir@atlasai.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: AtlasAI renewal — usage snapshot + capacity bridge proposal

Appreciate the clarity — that structure should work for us. Two items before we sign:

1) Can you send the DocuSign and the one-page mutual action plan? Procurement will need milestones and acceptance criteria.
2) Please include the latency note / p95 evidence for the three endpoints. We want to keep the rollout dependent on the short-stint Dedicated validation.

If both are included we can route to procurement this afternoon and come back with a signed amendment by Friday.

I'll expect the DocuSign link and MAP.

Best,
Helen
